stimulus.body: Source note: Koppen classes and their letters.

questions.stem: A source note for district 58 counts 6 Koppen groups listed in a table; if each has 2 subtypes, how many subtypes total?
questions.explanation: Six groups times two subtypes equals twelve subtypes. The tempting idea of adding groups and subtypes fails because total requires multiplication.

questions.subject: HUMAN_GEOGRAPHY
questions.topic: Decoding a climate class from two figures
questions.learningObjective: Decode a climate class from two figures.

stimulus.body: A station reports 12 C mean annual temperature and 600 mm annual rainfall. Planners must decode its climate class from these two figures.

questions.stem: A note circulated on decoding a climate class from two figures says: "This choice correctly applies the geographic concept to the given situation" On that basis, which class these figures suggest; what is it?

options.text: This choice ignores the role of distance in shaping observed outcomes.
options.misconception: ignores the role of distance in shaping observed outcomes

options.text: This choice correctly applies the geographic concept to the given situation.
This choice treats a local exception as the general rule for all cases.
options.misconception: treats a local exception as the general rule for all cases

options.text: This choice confuses the spatial pattern with a temporal trend in the data.
options.misconception: confuses spatial pattern with temporal trend in the data

questions.explanation: Cool temperature and moderate rainfall suggest a temperate or continental class. The tempting idea of using temperature alone fails because rainfall matters too.
